title: Development of a biodegradable active‐intelligent packaging film based on gelatin, oxidized sodium alginate, and blueberry anthocyanins reinforced with tea polyphenols for food preservation
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

To prolong the shelf life of fresh food, a biodegradable active-intelligent packaging film (G-OSA–BA–TP) was prepared by incorporating tea polyphenols (TP) into a covalently cross-linked matrix composed of gelatin-oxidized sodium alginate (G-OSA) and blueberry anthocyanins (BA).

RESULTS

Tea polyphenols were immobilized in the film-forming matrix through intermolecular hydrogen bonding. The synergistic effects of strengthened intermolecular hydrogen bonding and covalent cross-linking substantially improved the water barrier properties, mechanical properties, thermal stability, and functionality of the composite film. Notably, the water contact angle (WCA) reached a maximum of 132.4° in G-OSA–BA–TP2, which was nearly twice that of the pure gelatin film (67.9°). The G-OSA–BA–TP films exhibited excellent ultraviolet (UV) shielding (100% UV blocking), antioxidant activity (90.7% against the 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical), and antibacterial activity (maximum inhibition zones of 18.47 mm against Staphylococcus aureus (gram-positive) and 17.39 mm against Escherichia coli (gram-negative)). Incorporation of appropriate TP concentrations (2% to 3%, w/w, based on the dry weight of gelatin) endowed the films with good sustained-release capability and excellent ammonia responsiveness. When used to monitor shrimp freshness at 4 °C, the G-OSA–BA–TP2 film changed from brick red (fresh shrimp) to yellowish-green (spoiled shrimp) on day 4, exhibiting a pronounced color difference (ΔE > 20). When used to package shrimp and strawberries, the G-OSA–BA–TP3 film extended the shelf life of shrimp from approximately 3 days (unwrapped group) to approximately 5 days at 4 °C and maintained the relative freshness of strawberries until day 5 at 25 °C and 75% relative humidity (RH).

CONCLUSION

The biodegradable G-OSA–BA–TP film shows promise as an active-intelligent packaging material for food preservation. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
